mechanism_narrative: The observed week-on-week increase in RETAIL_REC mobility from t-1w to t-0w indicates a sustained positive momentum in consumer activity that will continue to drive retail footfall higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days, indicating a reversal of the recent upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained recovery in WORKPLACES mobility, indicated by its value rising above -15% from baseline, signifies a return to office-based work which directly increases demand for nearby retail and recreation services over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility remains above -15% but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase relative to the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: As people spend less time at home (RESIDENTIAL decreasing) and increasingly visit outdoor spaces (PARKS increasing), this shift in behavior towards out-of-home activities will spill over into retail and recreation, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL decreases while PARKS increases week-on-week
failure_condition: Despite RESIDENTIAL decreasing and PARKS increasing, RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is lower than the average of the last 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility suggests an underlying easing of public health policies, which will reduce barriers to movement and encourage greater retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES continue their recovery but RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 28 days, the policy easing effect is not translating to retail.

mechanism_narrative: If the recent positive momentum in RETAIL_REC reverses and falls below -25% from baseline, it signals a renewed decline in consumer confidence or activity, leading to a further decrease in retail and recreation mobility over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC falls below -25% from baseline but then recovers or remains stable in the following week, rather than decreasing further.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent week-on-week decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates a sustained trend of people spending less time at home, which inherently translates to more out-of-home activities including retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility continues to decline, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean of the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in TRANSIT usage combined with a recovery in GROCERY_PHARM mobility suggests a broader return to essential out-of-home activities and public transport, which will subsequently encourage more discretionary retail and recreation visits over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and GROCERY_PHARM both show week-on-week increases
failure_condition: TRANSIT and GROCERY_PHARM both increase week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not improve relative to the last 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: The significant rebound in PARKS mobility in the latest week suggests the onset of more favorable weather conditions, a seasonal factor that typically encourages more outdoor activities and general out-of-home movement, benefiting retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility shows a strong week-on-week increase (>5 points)
failure_condition: PARKS mobility increases significantly, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not improve, indicating that seasonal outdoor activity does not translate to retail.
